title: Schema compatibility audit harness for shadow/eval canaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable audit harness that runs alongside canary and shadow rollouts to validate structured output and function-call compatibility. The harness will compute both syntactic diffs and semantic drift scores for tool-calling schemas and structured JSON outputs, surface per-route/consumer compatibility metrics in the Console, and trigger automated rollback or traffic-routing changes when compatibility regressions exceed thresholds. This is intended to make canary and A/B rollouts safer for models that may change function-call signatures or structured output shapes.
motivation: We keep seeing small schema/field changes slip through canaries because traditional token-level metrics (perplexity) don't reflect breaking changes in toolcall shapes. Customers and internal integrations rely on stable function-call contracts. A fast, automated compatibility guard will reduce incidents, shorten validation cycles, and enable safer progressive rollouts for model variants and quantized builds.
scope: Implement runtime sidecar validator for shadow requests; diff engine for function-call parameters and structured JSON outputs; a drift scoring algorithm (syntactic + semantic); Console dashboard widgets; rollback policy integration with routing and rollout planner; e2e tests and migration guide for model on-call engineers.
out_of_scope: Full automatic schema migration tooling, complex programmatic repair of outputs, or integration with external contract registries in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar validator receives shadowed request/response pairs and emits compatibility events to telemetry
Compatibility events include: function-call existence diffs, param key diffs (added/removed/type-change), JSON-schema validation failures, and a summarized drift score
Console shows per-canary compatibility dashboard with heatmap by function and route
Automatic rollback policy can be configured by threshold (eg. >0.5 drift score or >0.2% breaking calls in 5m) and executes safe route fallback to previous compatible model
Test harness runs against 3 canonical prompt corpora and detects injected schema-breaking changes in synthetic runs
End-to-end latency overhead for shadow validation added by sidecar is <5ms p95 for typical requests
Documentation + runbook for on-call describing triage steps and how to unblock false positives
implementation_plan: Design event schema for compatibility findings (flat fields only) and add to existing telemetry pipeline

Prototype a sidecar validator that wires into the shadow traffic path and performs: (a) exact function-call signature check, (b) key-level JSON diff, (c) attempt simple semantic type normalization (strings->numbers where unambiguous)
Build a lightweight diff scoring algorithm: syntactic_weight*syntactic_score + semantic_weight*semantic_score; expose weights in config
Wire aggregated signals into Console: per-canary time series for breaking_call_rate, mean_drift_score, worst_function_by_occurrence
Integrate with rollout controller: add a compatibility gate that can mark canary unhealthy and switch traffic according to rollout policy
Author e2e tests that run the harness with a golden prompt set and simulated model variants that change schemas
Run an internal dogfood canary for two teams and iterate on false positive handling
testing_plan: Unit tests for diff engine (added/removed/renamed keys, type changes, nested-object diffs)
Property tests that randomly mutate function-call shapes to ensure score monotonicity
Integration test where shadowed requests are validated and compatibility events are consumed by the rollout controller
Performance test to measure sidecar overhead under typical batching conditions
Chaos test: inject intermittent validator failures and verify graceful degradation (validator errors should not drop production traffic)
Manual validation with feature teams using their real prompt corpora before enabling automated rollback
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert when breaking_call_rate > configured threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows
Dashboard panels: breaking_call_rate (per-route), mean_drift_score (P95), top-10 offending functions
SLO: Maintain <0.1% breaking calls during progressive rollout; alert on deviation
Audit log entries for every automated rollback with linked trace and sample payloads (redact PII)
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback if breaking_call_rate > 0.5% sustained for 1 minute
Soft rollback (pause or reduce traffic) if mean_drift_score > 0.6 for 5 minutes
Manual intervention mode for routes marked as high-sensitivity by product owners
Allow override with explanation and risk acknowledgement in Console; record as incident annotation
security_considerations: Compatibility events may include parameter names and sample (sanitized) payloads. Ensure PII is redacted before storage. Events should obey customer data residency policies for Private deployments. Sidecar runs in same trust boundary as model serving and must not escalate privileges.
docs_and_runbooks: Runbook: How to triage compatibility alerts and safe rollback steps
Developer guide: adding function-call contract metadata to model manifest for better diffing
open_questions: What are reasonable default weights for syntactic vs semantic scoring? (product decision)
How to represent intentionally deprecated fields vs accidental breaking changes in the score?
Should we support per-customer tolerances on Private deployments?
When is a semantic mismatch considered ‘non-breaking’ (eg. added optional field)?
notes: Avoid adding heavy ML-based semantic comparators in phase 1; focus on deterministic rules and a small set of heuristics. We'll instrument false positives during dogfood and iterate weights. Coordinate with Console team for the UX surface and with Observability team for storage/retention of compatibility events.
